user.title: Daikin D-BACS gateway
user.description: The address of the Daikin "Interface for use in BACnet" gateway. Everything is unicast, so no BACnet broadcast or BBMD configuration is needed. The connection is tested before the entry is created.

data_description.host: The gateway's IP address or hostname.
data_description.port: BACnet/IP port on the gateway. 47808 unless it was changed with Daikin's Trial Operation tool.
data_description.device_instance: Leave blank to learn it from a unicast Who-Is. Fill it in if the gateway does not answer — it is set with Daikin's Trial Operation tool.
data_description.local_address: The interface to bind, as address/prefix, for a host with more than one network. Leave blank to bind every interface.
data_description.local_port: The local UDP port to listen on. Change it if another BACnet client on this host already holds 47808.
data_description.our_instance: The BACnet device instance Home Assistant presents as. It must be unique on the network — not the gateway's, and not a head-end's.

error.scanning: The gateway is still scanning its DIII-NET network. Give it a minute and try again.

abort.already_configured: That gateway is already set up.

init.title: Points and timing
init.description: A fully expanded gateway could publish 256 indoor-unit groups of 33 readable points. Disabled points are never read and never subscribed, so this list is what decides the load on a gateway you are sharing with a building management system.

data.members: Points to carry, on every group
data.control: Allow Home Assistant to control the air conditioning
data.gated: Include the points that take control away from the room
data.min_write_interval: Minimum time between writes to one point

data_description.members: Chosen per point and applied to every group, present and future.
data_description.groups: Leave empty for every live group. Narrow it to switch a floor or a wing off wholesale.
data_description.scan_interval: How often every enabled point is read. The sweep is the safety net; change-of-value carries what needs to be live.
data_description.use_cov: Subscribe to run status, alarm, malfunction code and room temperature so they arrive as they change. The gateway allows five subscribers per point; a refusal falls back to the sweep.
data_description.cov_lifetime: Renewed before it lapses. Subscriptions are also rebuilt automatically if the gateway is power cycled, because it forgets them.
data_description.control: Off by default. With this on, each group gains a thermostat, a filter-reset button and switches for its other commands. Before any write, the integration reads the point's BACnet priority array and refuses if another client — usually the building management system — is holding it.
data_description.gated: Forced stop, forced thermostat off, and the three that disable the wall controller. These affect whoever is in the room rather than just a number on a dashboard, so they are left out unless you ask for them.
data_description.write_priority: 16 is the lowest and the right answer for a dashboard: anything the building's own control system holds sits above it and keeps working. Only lower this if you know what else writes to the gateway.
data_description.min_write_interval: Writes to the same point are spaced at least this far apart. A change that arrives sooner replaces the one already waiting, so nudging a setpoint twice sends one write rather than failing.
data_description.daily_write_cap: Daikin caps setting changes at 7,000 a year per point, which is 19 a day. An automation with a bad trigger would otherwise spend a year's allowance in an afternoon, and the result is a worn-out gateway rather than an error message.
data_description.enforce_write_cap: On by default. Turned off, the limit is only warned about in the log — the gateway's own hardware limit does not go away.
